reuse.why: Extends the existing shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend with a holidays parameter rather than writing a new mover, and reuses dayFromDate/addDays.

duplication.why: The 'weekend or holiday' predicate is written three times (isSkippedDay closure in getNextDate, the loop condition in getDateWithSkippedWeekend, and inline in getDatesInRange's daily branch) instead of one shared isSkippedDay helper.

placement.why: The moving rule lives in shared/schedules.ts where weekend handling already is, but the daily-skip check is still decided separately in server/schedules/app.ts.

scope.why: Only the type, recur-date parsing, the weekend helper and its callers plus tests are touched.

maintainability.why: Turning the helper into a generic loop is clean, but holidays must be remembered at every caller and the budget schedule-template callers were missed, so the rule is easy to apply inconsistently.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Callers still use getDateWithSkippedWeekend; the daily-skip check in app.ts getDatesInRange was already a local isWeekend check and stays local.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated weekend-or-holiday expression in schedules.ts getNextDate and schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange is openly repeated, not disguised.

one_place.where: The move rule lands in getDateWithSkippedWeekend, but holidays is an optional argument each caller must pass: budget/schedule-template.ts's two calls do not pass it, and the daily-skip holiday check is duplicated in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate and server/schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange.
